consensus_expectations: The corrected frozen FQ4 FY2026 bar is $12.09664bn revenue, up 12.8% from the matched FQ4 FY2025 $10.724bn, plus $3.42986 vendor-defined normalized EPS, up 15.1%; FY2026 consensus is $45.74358bn revenue, $13.21574 normalized EPS and $32.19310bn vendor EBITDA. Contributor counts are reported as FQ4/FY2026 revenue 29/29 and 36/37, normalized EPS 31/31 and 38/40, and EBITDA 13/16 and 22/24. Long-term growth is 13.5% mean and 14.0% median. Target price is $416.20 mean and $420.00 median; a reliable high-low range is not available. Revisions are mixed: FY2026 last-month breadth is +26 revenue, +8 EBITDA and -16 GAAP EPS, while normalized-EPS breadth is +22. The estimate set was at least 43 days old on the decision date. The earnings/04 file's 18.9% revenue-growth comparison used the wrong prior-year quarter and is superseded by the run's audited 12.8% correction. [analyses/V_2026-09-23/final_thesis.md, §§4, 17; analyses/V_2026-09-23/earnings/04_guidance-consensus.md, §§1, 4-6]
market_implied_expectations: At the canonical $364.15 pool-verified but 26-trading-day-stale price, the reverse DCF says that, if 9.04% WACC is the right cost of capital, price requires 19.67% annual FCF growth for five years, a 17.2% revenue CAGR to about $101.1bn in FY2031, annual revenue growth of 21.02%/19.02%/17.02%/15.02%/14.02%, and the model's held-fixed 63.0% EBIT margin. The same modeled base cash-flow path reconciles to price at a lower 7.15% implied WACC, 1.89 percentage points below the model rate. The priced-in read is therefore a demanding conditional hurdle, not proof of mispricing. [analyses/V_2026-09-23/valuation/05_reverse-dcf.md, §§1-5]
engine_view: The engine's 12-month bull/base/bear values are $425.88/$331.56/$283.37 with judgment probabilities of 20%/50%/30%. The base assumes $34.971bn of NTM vendor EBITDA at 18.338x, bridged with $11.499bn strict net debt, $514m preferred stock and 1.898bn diluted shares; the DCF cross-check's FY2027-FY2031 revenue-growth path is 12%/10%/8%/6%/5% with EBIT margin rising from 62.5% to 63.0%. The probability-weighted target is $335.97 and expected return is -7.74%. The $331.56 base is 75% multiples-led and 25% DCF, while independent values span $243.23-$367.62. [analyses/V_2026-09-23/final_thesis.md, §§6, 8, 14; analyses/V_2026-09-23/valuation/99_valuation-synthesis.md, §§2-5; analyses/V_2026-09-23/valuation/05_reverse-dcf.md, §2]
what_everyone_knows: Visa has a powerful asset-light global payment network. June-2026 LTM revenue grew 14.4%; Q3 payment volume and processed transactions each grew 10% on the stated comparable basis; and revenue plus vendor-defined normalized EPS beat consensus in each of the last four reported quarters. Four observations are a judgmental prior, not an empirical base rate. [analyses/V_2026-09-23/final_thesis.md, §4]
what_is_priced_in: The $364.15 anchor already reflects high growth and durable margins: at 9.04% WACC, the price requires roughly 19.67% five-year FCF growth and revenue reaching about $101.1bn while the modeled EBIT margin remains 63.0%. Alternatively, accepting the engine's base cash-flow path requires a 7.15% WACC. Current peer and own-history reference values of $367.62 and $355.21 also sit close to price, so the market is not offering an obvious relative-valuation discount. [analyses/V_2026-09-23/valuation/05_reverse-dcf.md, §§2-5; analyses/V_2026-09-23/valuation/99_valuation-synthesis.md, §§2-3]
what_market_may_be_missing: The engine's hypothesis is that the market may be underweighting the quality of recent growth: Q3 client incentives rose 18% against 14% net-revenue growth, Q3 GAAP-derived EBITDA margin fell 157 basis points to 62.3%, and LTM CFO fell 3.9% while revenue rose 14.4%. The cause of the cash divergence is not proven from available data, and these disclosed figures do not themselves prove the market is ignoring them. [analyses/V_2026-09-23/final_thesis.md, §§4-5]
evidence_engine_is_different: There is no proven variant perception yet. The filing-based incentive, margin and cash-conversion evidence supports a testable caution, but no evidence proves consensus is underweighting it; four recent revenue and normalized-EPS beats point the other way. Differential proof would require the filed FY2026 result: revenue at or below $11.85471bn, GAAP-derived EBITDA margin below 60.3%, or further CFO/EBITDA deterioration would support the caution, while revenue at or above $12.33857bn, margin at or above 60.3%, and better full-year cash conversion would weaken it. [analyses/V_2026-09-23/final_thesis.md, §§4, 10]
base_rate_check: The price-implied 19.67% five-year FCF CAGR is 9.3 percentage points above Visa's 10.4% FY2021-FY2025 reported-FCF CAGR, while LTM FCF fell 4.8%. The implied 17.2% revenue CAGR is also above the 13.5% FY2021-FY2025 revenue CAGR and 14.4% LTM growth. These matched metric, company and period comparisons make the 9.04%-WACC price path a stretch, not a forecast. The engine's central EBITDA assumption is consensus rather than exceptional, but its negative quality hypothesis is also unproven because it rests on recent margin/cash signals whose cause is not disclosed. [analyses/V_2026-09-23/valuation/05_reverse-dcf.md, §3; analyses/V_2026-09-23/final_thesis.md, §§4, 8]
notes: The signed base-value gap is ($331.56 / $364.15) - 1 = -8.949609%. It is not robust: the $364.15 pool price is stale, a fresh $361.52 quote is only indicative, the independent-method field spans $243.23-$367.62 (51.14% relative to the low), and a 7.15% WACC reconciles the modeled cash path to price. Edge score stays 35 because primary evidence makes the growth-quality concern real, but no differential proof establishes that the market is missing it or that the gap will close. The final thesis is also explicitly PROVISIONAL after a finish-gate Material-issues verdict (integrity 56/100). Single most important read: the modest negative valuation gap is not an exploitable edge without filed FY2026 proof. [analyses/V_2026-09-23/final_thesis.md, opening warning and §§1, 4, 6; analyses/V_2026-09-23/valuation/99_valuation-synthesis.md, §§1-5]
